findings.description: Session tokens remain valid on the server after the user logs out. An attacker who captures a session token before logout can reuse it indefinitely.
findings._x_remediation: Invalidate session tokens server-side upon logout. Ensure the session store removes or expires the session record. Do not rely solely on clearing the client-side cookie.

findings.title: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF)
findings.remediation_brief: Implement CSRF tokens (synchronizer token pattern or double-submit cookie). Use SameSite=Strict or SameSite=Lax cookies. Validate the Origin/Referer header for state-changing requests.
findings.description: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) was detected. State-changing requests lack CSRF tokens or other anti-CSRF mechanisms. An attacker can craft a malicious page that triggers state-changing actions in the victim's authenticated session.
findings._x_remediation: Implement CSRF tokens (synchronizer token pattern or double-submit cookie). Use SameSite=Strict or SameSite=Lax cookies. Validate the Origin/Referer header for state-changing requests.

findings.title: CSRF Token Not Validated Server-Side
findings.remediation_brief: Validate CSRF tokens server-side on every state-changing request. Reject requests with missing, empty, or invalid CSRF tokens. Ensure tokens are unpredictable and bound to the user session.
findings.description: The application includes CSRF tokens in forms but does not validate them server-side, or accepts any non-empty value as valid. The CSRF protection mechanism is present but ineffective.
findings._x_remediation: Validate CSRF tokens server-side on every state-changing request. Reject requests with missing, empty, or invalid CSRF tokens. Ensure tokens are unpredictable and bound to the user session.

findings.title: Cross-User Data Leakage
findings.remediation_brief: Implement strict data isolation per user/tenant. Audit all data access paths for ownership validation. Review caching configurations to prevent cross-user cache poisoning.
findings.description: Data belonging to one user is visible to another user due to insufficient isolation in shared resources, caches, or multi-tenant data stores. This is a class of broken access control.
findings._x_remediation: Implement strict data isolation per user/tenant. Audit all data access paths for ownership validation. Review caching configurations to prevent cross-user cache poisoning.

findings.title: Open Redirect
findings.remediation_brief: Validate redirect destinations against a strict whitelist of allowed URLs or origins. Avoid user-controlled redirect targets entirely. Use relative redirects where possible.
findings.description: An open redirect vulnerability was detected. The application redirects users to a URL specified in a request parameter without validation. Attackers can craft URLs that redirect victims to malicious sites, facilitating phishing.
findings._x_remediation: Validate redirect destinations against a strict whitelist of allowed URLs or origins. Avoid user-controlled redirect targets entirely. Use relative redirects where possible.

findings.title: Insecure Deserialization
findings.remediation_brief: Do not deserialize data from untrusted sources. Sign serialized objects with an HMAC and verify the signature before deserialization. Use safe serialization formats (JSON) instead of language-native object serialization.
findings.description: Insecure deserialization was detected. The application deserializes user-supplied data (via pickle, Java ObjectInputStream, PHP unserialize, YAML.load, etc.) without integrity verification. This can lead to remote code execution, authentication bypass, or denial of service.
findings._x_remediation: Do not deserialize data from untrusted sources. Sign serialized objects with an HMAC and verify the signature before deserialization. Use safe serialization formats (JSON) instead of language-native object serialization.

findings.title: Java Deserialization via Gadget Chains
findings.remediation_brief: Upgrade all Java serialization libraries to patched versions. Implement a serialization filter (JEP 290). Use Contrast Security or similar RASP to detect deserialization attacks at runtime.
findings.description: Java object deserialization was identified with known gadget chain exploitability. Exploitation of known gadget chains (Commons Collections, Spring, etc.) via ysoserial payloads can result in remote code execution.
findings._x_remediation: Upgrade all Java serialization libraries to patched versions. Implement a serialization filter (JEP 290). Use Contrast Security or similar RASP to detect deserialization attacks at runtime.

findings.title: PHP Object Injection via unserialize()
findings.remediation_brief: Never call unserialize() on user-supplied input. Replace with JSON or other data formats. If unavoidable, use allowed_classes parameter to restrict which classes can be instantiated.
findings.description: PHP's unserialize() function is called on user-controlled input. If the application's autoloaded classes contain exploitable magic methods (__wakeup, __destruct, __toString), this can lead to arbitrary code execution via POP chains.
findings._x_remediation: Never call unserialize() on user-supplied input. Replace with JSON or other data formats. If unavoidable, use allowed_classes parameter to restrict which classes can be instantiated.

findings.title: Unrestricted File Upload — Executable File
findings.remediation_brief: Implement a strict file extension whitelist for uploads. Validate file content using magic bytes, not just extension. Store uploaded files outside the web root. Rename all uploaded files to remove their original extension.
findings.description: The file upload functionality allows uploading of executable files (PHP, JSP, ASP, Python, etc.) without restriction. An attacker can upload a web shell and execute arbitrary commands on the server.
findings._x_remediation: Implement a strict file extension whitelist for uploads. Validate file content using magic bytes, not just extension. Store uploaded files outside the web root. Rename all uploaded files to remove their original extension.

findings.title: Unrestricted File Upload — MIME Type Bypass
findings.remediation_brief: Validate files using server-side magic byte analysis (file signature), not MIME type headers or extensions supplied by the client. Use a library such as python-magic or libmagic.
findings.description: The file upload validation relies solely on the Content-Type header or file extension, which can be manipulated by an attacker. Malicious file content can be uploaded while disguising it as a permitted MIME type.
findings._x_remediation: Validate files using server-side magic byte analysis (file signature), not MIME type headers or extensions supplied by the client. Use a library such as python-magic or libmagic.

findings.title: File Upload — Path Traversal in Filename
findings.remediation_brief: Never use client-supplied filenames for server-side storage. Generate a random server-side filename for every uploaded file. Strip all path components from the original filename.
findings.description: The file upload functionality uses the client-supplied filename in the server-side file path without sanitization. An attacker can supply a filename with path traversal sequences to write files to arbitrary server locations.
findings._x_remediation: Never use client-supplied filenames for server-side storage. Generate a random server-side filename for every uploaded file. Strip all path components from the original filename.

findings.title: Mass Assignment Vulnerability
findings.remediation_brief: Implement an explicit allowlist of fields that can be mass-assigned from user input. Use Data Transfer Objects (DTOs) or explicit field binding rather than mapping all request parameters to model attributes.
findings.description: Mass assignment (also known as auto-binding) was detected. The application binds HTTP request parameters directly to internal model attributes without filtering. An attacker can set privileged attributes (isAdmin, role, balance) by adding them to the request body.
findings._x_remediation: Implement an explicit allowlist of fields that can be mass-assigned from user input. Use Data Transfer Objects (DTOs) or explicit field binding rather than mapping all request parameters to model attributes.

findings.title: Mass Assignment — Privilege Escalation via Role Field
findings.remediation_brief: Block mass assignment of privilege-related fields. Explicitly whitelist only user-modifiable fields. Validate and enforce role changes through dedicated privileged endpoints.
findings.description: Mass assignment was exploited to modify a privileged field such as 'isAdmin', 'role', or 'permission_level' by including it in a user-controlled request body. This allows privilege escalation to administrator or higher-privileged roles.
findings._x_remediation: Block mass assignment of privilege-related fields. Explicitly whitelist only user-modifiable fields. Validate and enforce role changes through dedicated privileged endpoints.

findings.title: Broken Object-Level Authorization (BOLA) in API
findings.remediation_brief: Implement authorization checks at the object level for every API endpoint. Validate that the authenticated user has permission to access the specific object referenced in the request.
findings.description: API endpoints expose object-level access without authorization validation. An authenticated user can access or modify another user's objects by substituting object IDs in API requests (equivalent to IDOR in APIs).
findings._x_remediation: Implement authorization checks at the object level for every API endpoint. Validate that the authenticated user has permission to access the specific object referenced in the request.

findings.title: Broken Function-Level Authorization (BFLA) in API
findings.remediation_brief: Enforce role-based access control at the function/endpoint level. Apply authorization middleware to every API route that requires privilege. Perform authorization checks server-side on every request.
findings.description: API endpoints with administrative or privileged functionality are accessible to lower-privileged or unauthenticated users. Function-level access control is not enforced by the API.
findings._x_remediation: Enforce role-based access control at the function/endpoint level. Apply authorization middleware to every API route that requires privilege. Perform authorization checks server-side on every request.

findings.title: HTTP Method Override Accepted
findings.remediation_brief: Disable HTTP method override support unless explicitly required. If required, restrict method overrides to authenticated users and validate that the overridden method is appropriate for the endpoint.
findings.description: The application accepts HTTP method override headers (X-HTTP-Method-Override, X-Method-Override) that substitute the actual HTTP method with a client-specified one. This may bypass access controls that rely on HTTP method restrictions.
findings._x_remediation: Disable HTTP method override support unless explicitly required. If required, restrict method overrides to authenticated users and validate that the overridden method is appropriate for the endpoint.

findings.title: CORS Misconfiguration — Arbitrary Origin Reflected
findings.remediation_brief: Maintain an explicit whitelist of allowed origins. Never reflect the request Origin blindly. Do not combine Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true with dynamic origin reflection or wildcard origins.
findings.description: The server reflects the request's Origin header in the Access-Control-Allow-Origin response header and includes Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true. This allows any origin to make credentialed cross-origin requests and read responses, bypassing the Same-Origin Policy.
findings._x_remediation: Maintain an explicit whitelist of allowed origins. Never reflect the request Origin blindly. Do not combine Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true with dynamic origin reflection or wildcard origins.

findings.title: CORS Misconfiguration — Null Origin Allowed
findings.remediation_brief: Remove 'null' from the allowed origins list. Use an explicit origin whitelist instead.
findings.description: The server includes 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin: null' in its response. This allows sandboxed iframes, redirects, and local file requests to make credentialed cross-origin requests to the API.
findings._x_remediation: Remove 'null' from the allowed origins list. Use an explicit origin whitelist instead.

findings.title: Business Logic Flaw — Negative Value Accepted
findings.remediation_brief: Validate that all numeric inputs are within expected positive ranges. Apply server-side bounds checking for all quantity, price, and amount fields.
findings.description: The application accepts negative numeric values in business-critical fields (quantity, price, payment amount). This can be exploited to inflate balances, receive credit for purchases, or bypass monetary validation.
findings._x_remediation: Validate that all numeric inputs are within expected positive ranges. Apply server-side bounds checking for all quantity, price, and amount fields.

findings.title: Business Logic Flaw — Price Manipulation
findings.remediation_brief: Never trust client-submitted prices. Fetch prices from the server-side data store using product IDs and compute totals server-side. Treat price as a read-only server-computed field.
findings.description: The application trusts client-submitted pricing data without server-side verification. An attacker can manipulate price parameters to purchase items at an arbitrary price.
findings._x_remediation: Never trust client-submitted prices. Fetch prices from the server-side data store using product IDs and compute totals server-side. Treat price as a read-only server-computed field.

findings.title: Business Logic Flaw — Coupon/Discount Abuse
findings.remediation_brief: Enforce server-side usage limits per coupon and per user. Validate coupon applicability rules on the server. Implement transactional locks to prevent race condition exploitation.
findings.description: Coupon or discount codes can be applied multiple times per order, stacked beyond intended limits, or applied to ineligible items. Insufficient validation allows financial loss through discount abuse.
findings._x_remediation: Enforce server-side usage limits per coupon and per user. Validate coupon applicability rules on the server. Implement transactional locks to prevent race condition exploitation.

findings.title: Business Logic Flaw — Workflow Step Bypass
findings.remediation_brief: Track workflow state server-side and enforce step ordering. Verify prerequisites are complete before allowing advancement to subsequent steps.
findings.description: Multi-step workflows (checkout, verification, approval) can be bypassed by directly accessing later steps without completing earlier steps. Server-side workflow state is not enforced.
findings._x_remediation: Track workflow state server-side and enforce step ordering. Verify prerequisites are complete before allowing advancement to subsequent steps.

findings.title: Business Logic Flaw — Race Condition
findings.remediation_brief: Implement database-level row locking or optimistic concurrency control for critical operations. Use atomic transactions. Implement idempotency keys to prevent duplicate processing.
findings.description: A race condition was detected in a critical business operation (e.g., balance check-then-debit, coupon redemption, token verification). Concurrent requests can cause the operation to be performed multiple times before state is updated.
findings._x_remediation: Implement database-level row locking or optimistic concurrency control for critical operations. Use atomic transactions. Implement idempotency keys to prevent duplicate processing.

findings.title: Rate Limiting Not Enforced on Sensitive Endpoint
findings.remediation_brief: Implement per-IP and per-user rate limiting on all sensitive endpoints. Use exponential backoff or CAPTCHA challenges after threshold violations.
findings.description: No rate limiting is applied to sensitive endpoints such as OTP verification, coupon redemption, password reset, or API calls. Attackers can make unlimited requests to brute-force codes or automate abuse.
findings._x_remediation: Implement per-IP and per-user rate limiting on all sensitive endpoints. Use exponential backoff or CAPTCHA challenges after threshold violations.

findings.title: Insecure Direct Object Reference in File Download
findings.remediation_brief: Validate file ownership on every download request. Use indirect file references (GUIDs) instead of filesystem paths. Sanitize filenames and resolve canonical paths before access.
findings.description: File download endpoints use user-supplied filenames or IDs to retrieve files without ownership validation or path sanitization. Users can download files belonging to other users or access arbitrary files on the filesystem.
findings._x_remediation: Validate file ownership on every download request. Use indirect file references (GUIDs) instead of filesystem paths. Sanitize filenames and resolve canonical paths before access.

findings.title: Screenshot Captured — Web Application Surface
findings.remediation_brief: No remediation required. Informational finding for documentation purposes.
findings.description: A screenshot of the target web application was captured. This records the visual surface of the application for documentation and change tracking purposes.
findings._x_remediation: No remediation required. Informational finding for documentation purposes.

findings.title: FFUF Directory/File Discovered
findings.remediation_brief: Review discovered paths and apply appropriate access controls. Remove any paths that expose sensitive content or unused functionality.
findings.description: Content discovery via ffuf identified a directory or file not linked from the main application. Hidden paths may contain sensitive functionality, backups, or configuration files.
findings._x_remediation: Review discovered paths and apply appropriate access controls. Remove any paths that expose sensitive content or unused functionality.

findings.title: FFUF — Administrative Path Discovered
findings.remediation_brief: Restrict access to administrative paths by IP whitelist, VPN, or network segmentation. Enforce strong authentication on all administrative endpoints.
findings.description: ffuf content discovery identified an administrative interface or control panel at a predictable path. Administrative paths accessible without authentication represent a critical security risk.
findings._x_remediation: Restrict access to administrative paths by IP whitelist, VPN, or network segmentation. Enforce strong authentication on all administrative endpoints.

findings.title: shcheck — Missing Security Header
findings.remediation_brief: Implement the missing security headers identified by shcheck. Refer to the OWASP Secure Headers Project for recommended header values and configurations.
findings.description: Security header analysis via shcheck identified one or more missing or misconfigured HTTP security headers. Missing security headers increase exposure to common browser-based attacks.
findings._x_remediation: Implement the missing security headers identified by shcheck. Refer to the OWASP Secure Headers Project for recommended header values and configurations.

findings.title: Crawl — Undocumented Endpoint Discovered
findings.remediation_brief: Review all discovered endpoints and ensure they are properly secured and documented. Remove or disable any endpoints that are no longer required.
findings.description: Application crawling discovered an endpoint not listed in sitemap.xml, robots.txt, or API documentation. Undocumented endpoints may contain legacy, debug, or unprotected functionality.
findings._x_remediation: Review all discovered endpoints and ensure they are properly secured and documented. Remove or disable any endpoints that are no longer required.

findings.title: Crawl — External Domain Reference Found
findings.remediation_brief: Audit all external resource dependencies. Use Subresource Integrity (SRI) hashes for external scripts and stylesheets. Consider self-hosting critical dependencies.
findings.description: The application references external domains for resources (CDNs, third-party scripts, fonts). External dependencies introduce supply chain risk if those domains are compromised or the resources are modified.
findings._x_remediation: Audit all external resource dependencies. Use Subresource Integrity (SRI) hashes for external scripts and stylesheets. Consider self-hosting critical dependencies.

findings.title: TLS Certificate Transparency Log Entry
findings.remediation_brief: Informational. Review discovered subdomains for security implications. Ensure all discovered subdomains are accounted for and secured.
findings.description: Certificate Transparency logs reveal all certificates issued for the target domain and its subdomains. This information exposes the full scope of the application's TLS-protected surface.
findings._x_remediation: Informational. Review discovered subdomains for security implications. Ensure all discovered subdomains are accounted for and secured.

findings.title: Authentication — Concurrent Session Not Restricted
findings.remediation_brief: Implement concurrent session controls with configurable limits. Notify users of new sessions and provide session management (view and terminate active sessions).
findings.description: The application allows unlimited concurrent sessions for a single user account. This makes it impossible to detect or prevent session sharing or account compromise based on active session count.
findings._x_remediation: Implement concurrent session controls with configurable limits. Notify users of new sessions and provide session management (view and terminate active sessions).

findings.title: HTTP Methods — Dangerous Methods Enabled (PUT/DELETE/TRACE)
findings.remediation_brief: Disable unused HTTP methods at the web server level. Explicitly allow only the HTTP methods required by the application. Disable TRACE globally.
findings.description: The web server responds to dangerous HTTP methods including PUT (file upload), DELETE (file deletion), or TRACE (XST — Cross-Site Tracing). These methods may enable unauthorized modification of server content or session token theft.
findings._x_remediation: Disable unused HTTP methods at the web server level. Explicitly allow only the HTTP methods required by the application. Disable TRACE globally.

findings.title: Clickjacking Vulnerability
findings.remediation_brief: Add 'X-Frame-Options: DENY' or 'Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors none' to all application responses. Use the CSP frame-ancestors directive for more granular control.
findings.description: The application does not implement anti-clickjacking protections (X-Frame-Options or CSP frame-ancestors). The page can be embedded in an attacker-controlled iframe to trick users into performing unintended actions.
findings._x_remediation: Add 'X-Frame-Options: DENY' or 'Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors none' to all application responses. Use the CSP frame-ancestors directive for more granular control.

findings.title: Sensitive Data Exposure — PII in Response
findings.remediation_brief: Implement response filtering to include only fields necessary for the requesting user's context. Apply data minimization principles. Ensure sensitive fields are encrypted at rest and masked in API responses.
findings.description: API responses or page content expose personally identifiable information (PII) such as email addresses, phone numbers, SSNs, or financial data that should not be visible to the requesting user or at all.
findings._x_remediation: Implement response filtering to include only fields necessary for the requesting user's context. Apply data minimization principles. Ensure sensitive fields are encrypted at rest and masked in API responses.

findings.title: Insecure Password Storage (Cleartext or Weak Hash)
findings.remediation_brief: Store passwords using a modern adaptive hashing algorithm (bcrypt, Argon2id, or scrypt) with an appropriate cost factor. Never store passwords in cleartext or using reversible encryption.
findings.description: Evidence suggests passwords are stored in cleartext, as reversible encryption, or using a weak unsalted hash algorithm (MD5, SHA-1). Password compromise leads to immediate credential exposure.
findings._x_remediation: Store passwords using a modern adaptive hashing algorithm (bcrypt, Argon2id, or scrypt) with an appropriate cost factor. Never store passwords in cleartext or using reversible encryption.

findings.title: Subdomain Takeover — S3 Bucket Not Found
findings.remediation_brief: Delete the dangling CNAME record or create and properly configure the S3 bucket. Implement S3 bucket name reservation for subdomains.
findings.description: A subdomain's DNS CNAME points to an AWS S3 bucket that returns a NoSuchBucket error. An attacker can create an S3 bucket with the matching name and serve content from the trusted subdomain.
findings._x_remediation: Delete the dangling CNAME record or create and properly configure the S3 bucket. Implement S3 bucket name reservation for subdomains.

findings.title: Subdomain Takeover — GitHub Pages
findings.remediation_brief: Remove the dangling CNAME record. If GitHub Pages are still required, recreate the repository and verify the custom domain configuration.
findings.description: A subdomain's DNS CNAME points to a GitHub Pages site that no longer exists or is unclaimed. An attacker can create a matching GitHub repository with Pages enabled to take over the subdomain.
findings._x_remediation: Remove the dangling CNAME record. If GitHub Pages are still required, recreate the repository and verify the custom domain configuration.

findings.title: Subdomain Takeover — Heroku
findings.remediation_brief: Remove the dangling DNS record. If the Heroku app is still required, redeploy it and verify the custom domain binding.
findings.description: A subdomain's DNS CNAME points to a Heroku application that has been deleted or is unclaimed. An attacker can provision a new Heroku app with the matching domain to take over the subdomain.
findings._x_remediation: Remove the dangling DNS record. If the Heroku app is still required, redeploy it and verify the custom domain binding.

findings.title: Prototype Pollution in JavaScript
findings.remediation_brief: Sanitize keys before merging user-supplied objects. Use Object.create(null) for dictionaries. Validate that __proto__ and constructor keys are rejected in user input.
findings.description: Prototype pollution was detected. User-controlled JSON or query parameter keys such as __proto__, constructor, or prototype are merged into application objects, potentially polluting the JavaScript prototype chain and affecting all objects.
findings._x_remediation: Sanitize keys before merging user-supplied objects. Use Object.create(null) for dictionaries. Validate that __proto__ and constructor keys are rejected in user input.

findings.title: HTTP Request Smuggling
findings.remediation_brief: Ensure consistent HTTP parsing between all front-end and back-end components. Normalize ambiguous Transfer-Encoding headers at the edge. Upgrade to HTTP/2 where possible.
findings.description: HTTP request smuggling was detected due to inconsistent interpretation of Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding headers between the front-end proxy and back-end server. This can enable cache poisoning, request hijacking, or security control bypass.
findings._x_remediation: Ensure consistent HTTP parsing between all front-end and back-end components. Normalize ambiguous Transfer-Encoding headers at the edge. Upgrade to HTTP/2 where possible.

findings.title: Web Cache Poisoning
findings.remediation_brief: Review cache key configuration to include all headers that influence response content. Validate and sanitize headers before reflecting them in responses.
findings.description: Web cache poisoning was detected. The caching layer reflects unkeyed request headers (X-Forwarded-Host, X-Original-URL) into cached responses. An attacker can poison the cache to serve malicious content to all users.
findings._x_remediation: Review cache key configuration to include all headers that influence response content. Validate and sanitize headers before reflecting them in responses.

findings.title: GraphQL Authorization Bypass
findings.remediation_brief: Implement field-level authorization checks using a library such as graphql-shield. Apply authorization at the resolver level, not just the query level.
findings.description: GraphQL queries can access data from unauthorized objects or users by bypassing field-level authorization. Inline fragment spreading or alias tricks may circumvent per-field permission checks.
findings._x_remediation: Implement field-level authorization checks using a library such as graphql-shield. Apply authorization at the resolver level, not just the query level.

findings.title: Information Disclosure — Internal Path in Response
findings.remediation_brief: Configure custom error pages. Remove all internal path references from HTTP responses. Review template and error handling code for inadvertent path disclosure.
findings.description: Internal filesystem paths (e.g., /var/www/html/, C:\inetpub\wwwroot\) are disclosed in HTTP responses, error pages, or HTTP headers. These paths aid attackers in fingerprinting the server environment.
findings._x_remediation: Configure custom error pages. Remove all internal path references from HTTP responses. Review template and error handling code for inadvertent path disclosure.

findings.title: Access Matrix — Unauthenticated Access to Authenticated Endpoint
findings.remediation_brief: Implement authentication middleware that applies to all routes requiring login. Use a deny-by-default access control policy where routes must be explicitly marked as public.
findings.description: An endpoint designated as requiring authentication is accessible without any session token or authentication credentials. Authentication enforcement is missing for this route.
findings._x_remediation: Implement authentication middleware that applies to all routes requiring login. Use a deny-by-default access control policy where routes must be explicitly marked as public.

findings.title: Access Matrix — Lower-Role Access to Higher-Role Endpoint
findings.remediation_brief: Enforce role-based authorization on all privileged endpoints. Validate the user's role server-side on every request. Implement centralized authorization that cannot be bypassed.
findings.description: An endpoint restricted to a higher-privileged role (admin, manager) is accessible by a lower-privileged authenticated user. Role-based access control enforcement is missing or inadequate for this endpoint.
findings._x_remediation: Enforce role-based authorization on all privileged endpoints. Validate the user's role server-side on every request. Implement centralized authorization that cannot be bypassed.

findings.title: Access Matrix — User A Can Read User B Data
findings.remediation_brief: Validate object ownership on every read operation. Implement server-side checks that confirm the requesting user is authorized to view the specific object.
findings.description: Authenticated user A can read data owned by user B by manipulating object identifiers in API requests. Object-level authorization is not enforced for read operations.
findings._x_remediation: Validate object ownership on every read operation. Implement server-side checks that confirm the requesting user is authorized to view the specific object.

findings.title: Access Matrix — User A Can Modify User B Data
findings.remediation_brief: Validate object ownership on every write and delete operation. Require explicit ownership or permission grants before allowing modifications to another user's data.
findings.description: Authenticated user A can modify or delete data owned by user B by manipulating object identifiers in API requests. Object-level authorization is not enforced for write operations.
findings._x_remediation: Validate object ownership on every write and delete operation. Require explicit ownership or permission grants before allowing modifications to another user's data.

findings.title: Access Matrix — Admin Functionality Accessible by Regular User
findings.remediation_brief: Implement strict role-based access control with a separate administrative role. Enforce role checks at the API handler level for all administrative operations.
findings.description: Administrative functions (user management, system configuration, data export) are accessible to regular authenticated users without elevated privileges. The access control matrix has gaps in administrative endpoint protection.
findings._x_remediation: Implement strict role-based access control with a separate administrative role. Enforce role checks at the API handler level for all administrative operations.

findings.title: HTTP Security Header — X-Frame-Options Incorrectly Configured
findings.remediation_brief: Set X-Frame-Options to 'DENY' or 'SAMEORIGIN'. Validate the header value is correctly parsed by target browsers.
findings.description: The X-Frame-Options header is present but misconfigured (e.g., set to ALLOWALL or using an invalid value). An incorrect configuration may still allow the page to be framed, enabling clickjacking attacks.
findings._x_remediation: Set X-Frame-Options to 'DENY' or 'SAMEORIGIN'. Validate the header value is correctly parsed by target browsers.

findings.title: Content-Security-Policy — Unsafe-Eval Allowed
findings.remediation_brief: Remove 'unsafe-eval' from the CSP. Refactor code that relies on eval() to use safer alternatives. Review all dynamic code execution patterns.
findings.description: The Content-Security-Policy header contains 'unsafe-eval', which allows the use of eval(), setTimeout(), setInterval() with string arguments, and new Function(). This significantly weakens XSS protections.
findings._x_remediation: Remove 'unsafe-eval' from the CSP. Refactor code that relies on eval() to use safer alternatives. Review all dynamic code execution patterns.

findings.title: TLS Forward Secrecy Not Supported
findings.remediation_brief: Enable ECDHE (Elliptic Curve Diffie-Hellman Ephemeral) cipher suites. Disable static RSA key exchange. Prefer ECDHE-RSA or ECDHE-ECDSA cipher suites.
findings.description: The server does not support cipher suites that provide Perfect Forward Secrecy (PFS). Without PFS, a compromise of the server's private key allows decryption of all previously captured TLS sessions.
findings._x_remediation: Enable ECDHE (Elliptic Curve Diffie-Hellman Ephemeral) cipher suites. Disable static RSA key exchange. Prefer ECDHE-RSA or ECDHE-ECDSA cipher suites.

findings.title: TLS OCSP Stapling Not Configured
findings.remediation_brief: Enable OCSP stapling in the web server configuration (ssl_stapling on in Nginx; SSLUseStapling on in Apache). Include the OCSP stapling cache configuration.
findings.description: OCSP stapling is not configured on the server. Without stapling, clients must query the OCSP responder directly to check certificate revocation status, introducing latency and potential privacy leakage.
findings._x_remediation: Enable OCSP stapling in the web server configuration (ssl_stapling on in Nginx; SSLUseStapling on in Apache). Include the OCSP stapling cache configuration.

findings.title: GraphQL SQL Injection via Argument
findings.remediation_brief: Use parameterized queries or ORM methods in all GraphQL resolvers. Sanitize and validate all argument values. Apply input type constraints at the GraphQL schema level.
findings.description: SQL injection was detected via GraphQL query arguments. Unsanitized argument values are passed to underlying database queries without parameterization.
findings._x_remediation: Use parameterized queries or ORM methods in all GraphQL resolvers. Sanitize and validate all argument values. Apply input type constraints at the GraphQL schema level.

findings.title: Sensitive Data in GET Request Parameters
findings.remediation_brief: Transmit sensitive data via POST request bodies over HTTPS. Never include credentials, session tokens, or sensitive identifiers in URL query parameters.
findings.description: Sensitive data (passwords, session tokens, personal information) is transmitted in GET request query parameters. GET parameters are logged in server logs, browser history, and Referer headers, exposing sensitive values.
findings._x_remediation: Transmit sensitive data via POST request bodies over HTTPS. Never include credentials, session tokens, or sensitive identifiers in URL query parameters.

findings.title: Missing Rate Limiting on Password Reset
findings.remediation_brief: Implement rate limiting on the password reset endpoint (per IP and per account). Add CAPTCHA after a threshold of requests.
findings.description: The password reset endpoint does not enforce rate limiting. An attacker can repeatedly request password resets for target accounts, potentially triggering email flooding or token enumeration.
findings._x_remediation: Implement rate limiting on the password reset endpoint (per IP and per account). Add CAPTCHA after a threshold of requests.

findings.title: Insecure Redirect After Authentication
findings.remediation_brief: Validate post-login redirect URLs against a whitelist. Use relative paths for redirects. Never redirect to externally supplied URLs without validation.
findings.description: The post-authentication redirect URL is controlled by a user-supplied parameter (e.g., next=, redirect=, returnUrl=) without validation. An attacker can craft a phishing URL that redirects users to a malicious site after successful login.
findings._x_remediation: Validate post-login redirect URLs against a whitelist. Use relative paths for redirects. Never redirect to externally supplied URLs without validation.

findings.title: Lack of Security.txt File
findings.remediation_brief: Create a security.txt file at /.well-known/security.txt specifying contact information, disclosure policy, and PGP keys for secure communications.
findings.description: The application does not have a security.txt file at /.well-known/security.txt. The security.txt standard (RFC 9116) allows security researchers to identify and report vulnerabilities responsibly.
findings._x_remediation: Create a security.txt file at /.well-known/security.txt specifying contact information, disclosure policy, and PGP keys for secure communications.

findings.title: HTTP/2 Rapid Reset Attack Exposure
findings.remediation_brief: Apply patches from the web server vendor for CVE-2023-44487. Implement HTTP/2 stream limits and reset rate limiting. Update to a patched version of the HTTP/2 implementation.
findings.description: The server supports HTTP/2 and may be vulnerable to the HTTP/2 Rapid Reset attack (CVE-2023-44487). An attacker can open and cancel streams at high speed to cause resource exhaustion and denial of service.
findings._x_remediation: Apply patches from the web server vendor for CVE-2023-44487. Implement HTTP/2 stream limits and reset rate limiting. Update to a patched version of the HTTP/2 implementation.

findings.title: CDN Active
findings.remediation_brief: Restrict origin server to accept connections only from CDN IP ranges. Ensure security headers are set at the origin. Review CDN cache key configuration to prevent web cache poisoning.
findings.description: A Content Delivery Network (CDN) was identified in front of the target via response headers or Server fingerprinting. TLS findings reflect the CDN edge configuration. Cache poisoning may be in scope. Header values and security posture may differ at the origin server.
findings._x_remediation: Restrict origin server to accept connections only from CDN IP ranges. Ensure security headers are set at the origin. Review CDN cache key configuration to prevent web cache poisoning.

findings.title: WAF / Edge Security Platform Active
findings.remediation_brief: Keep WAF rule sets up to date covering OWASP Top 10 2025. Do not rely solely on WAF protection — fix underlying vulnerabilities. Review WAF bypass techniques relevant to the identified platform.
findings.description: A WAF or edge security platform was identified in front of the target via response headers or body signatures. WAF rules may suppress injection probes — absence of a finding does not confirm absence of the vulnerability. Bot-protection may interrupt automated probes.
findings._x_remediation: Keep WAF rule sets up to date covering OWASP Top 10 2025. Do not rely solely on WAF protection — fix underlying vulnerabilities. Review WAF bypass techniques relevant to the identified platform.

findings.title: WAF/CDN IP Block Detected
findings.remediation_brief: Rotate scanner IP or use authorized IP whitelisting for the pentest engagement. Notify the client if the scanner is being rate-limited or blocked.
findings.description: The WAF or CDN is blocking all requests from the scanner's IP address. All subsequent results from this point forward may be unreliable as every request returns a WAF block page.
findings._x_remediation: Rotate scanner IP or use authorized IP whitelisting for the pentest engagement. Notify the client if the scanner is being rate-limited or blocked.

findings.title: WAF/CDN Session Termination Detected
findings.remediation_brief: Re-authenticate and resume the scan. Consider using static session tokens or IP-whitelisting for the scanner in the WAF configuration.
findings.description: The WAF or CDN revoked the authenticated session mid-scan (HTTP 401 or login redirect returned on root URL probe). Authenticated scan results from this point may be incomplete.
findings._x_remediation: Re-authenticate and resume the scan. Consider using static session tokens or IP-whitelisting for the scanner in the WAF configuration.

findings.title: WAF/CDN Challenge Page Active
findings.remediation_brief: Request the client whitelist the scanner IP in the WAF configuration for the duration of the assessment.
findings.description: The WAF or CDN is serving a JavaScript challenge or CAPTCHA page instead of real content. Automated probe results may be incomplete or inaccurate while the challenge is active.
findings._x_remediation: Request the client whitelist the scanner IP in the WAF configuration for the duration of the assessment.

findings.title: Potential CDN Origin Bypass
findings.remediation_brief: Restrict origin server to accept connections only from CDN IP ranges. Implement firewall rules to block direct internet access to the origin.
findings.description: A request with IP spoofing headers (X-Forwarded-For, X-Real-IP) returned a different Server header, suggesting the origin server may be reachable without passing through the CDN. Direct access to the origin bypasses CDN-level WAF and rate-limiting.
findings._x_remediation: Restrict origin server to accept connections only from CDN IP ranges. Implement firewall rules to block direct internet access to the origin.

findings.title: Web Cache Poisoning
findings.remediation_brief: Ensure all headers that influence the response are included in the CDN cache key. Remove unkeyed header reflection from the application.
findings.description: An unkeyed request header was reflected in a cached response. An attacker can inject this header with a malicious value and have the CDN serve that value to all subsequent users who receive the cached response.
findings._x_remediation: Ensure all headers that influence the response are included in the CDN cache key. Remove unkeyed header reflection from the application.

findings.title: Wildcard (*) Detected
findings.remediation_brief: Review server-side routing to ensure 404 responses are returned for truly non-existent paths rather than wildcard catch-all responses.
findings.description: A wildcard/catch-all response was detected — the server returns the same response for all unknown paths. Directory brute-forcing may be unreliable; all path-based findings are validated against the wildcard baseline.
findings._x_remediation: Review server-side routing to ensure 404 responses are returned for truly non-existent paths rather than wildcard catch-all responses.

findings.title: CMS Detected
findings.remediation_brief: Ensure the CMS and all plugins/themes are kept up to date. Remove version disclosure from meta generator tags.
findings.description: A Content Management System (CMS) was identified from page source signatures, meta tags, or response headers. A known CMS allows attackers to target version-specific vulnerabilities and enumerate plugins/themes.
findings._x_remediation: Ensure the CMS and all plugins/themes are kept up to date. Remove version disclosure from meta generator tags.

findings.title: Web Structure Identified
findings.remediation_brief: No direct remediation required. Ensure the application exposes only necessary fingerprinting signals.
findings.description: The web application framework or structure type was classified (e.g., SPA, SSR Hybrid, Server-Rendered, Static HTML, API-first) from response characteristics. This informs subsequent testing phases.
findings._x_remediation: No direct remediation required. Ensure the application exposes only necessary fingerprinting signals.

findings.title: Single Page Application Detected
findings.remediation_brief: No direct remediation required.
findings.description: A Single Page Application (SPA) was identified. Client-side routing and dynamic content loading may prevent traditional crawler-based endpoint discovery. JavaScript analysis is used to supplement crawling.
findings._x_remediation: No direct remediation required.

findings.title: Sensitive Paths Disclosed in robots.txt
findings.remediation_brief: Remove sensitive paths from robots.txt. Use proper access controls to restrict access to sensitive areas rather than relying on search engine exclusion.
findings.description: The robots.txt file discloses path patterns intended to be hidden from search engines. These paths are still accessible by attackers and their disclosure aids reconnaissance.
findings._x_remediation: Remove sensitive paths from robots.txt. Use proper access controls to restrict access to sensitive areas rather than relying on search engine exclusion.

findings.title: Header Data Leakage: Server
findings.remediation_brief: Remove or genericise the Server response header in the web server configuration (e.g., ServerTokens Prod in Apache; server_tokens off in nginx).
findings.description: The HTTP Server response header reveals the web server software name and version, reducing the attacker's reconnaissance effort needed to identify version-specific vulnerabilities.
findings._x_remediation: Remove or genericise the Server response header in the web server configuration (e.g., ServerTokens Prod in Apache; server_tokens off in nginx).

findings.title: Header Data Leakage: X-Powered-By
findings.remediation_brief: Remove or suppress the X-Powered-By header at the application framework or reverse-proxy level.
findings.description: The X-Powered-By response header discloses the application framework, language, or runtime version, reducing the attacker's effort needed to identify version-specific vulnerabilities.
findings._x_remediation: Remove or suppress the X-Powered-By header at the application framework or reverse-proxy level.

findings.title: Header Data Leakage: X-AspNet-Version
findings.remediation_brief: Set <httpRuntime enableVersionHeader='false' /> in Web.config and configure the reverse proxy to strip this header.
findings.description: The X-AspNet-Version header discloses the exact .NET framework version in use, assisting attackers in identifying version-specific vulnerabilities.
findings._x_remediation: Set <httpRuntime enableVersionHeader='false' /> in Web.config and configure the reverse proxy to strip this header.

findings.title: Header Data Leakage: Via
findings.remediation_brief: Configure reverse proxies to suppress or genericise the Via header.
findings.description: The Via response header discloses internal proxy or gateway infrastructure details, including software versions and internal host names.
findings._x_remediation: Configure reverse proxies to suppress or genericise the Via header.

findings.title: Header Data Leakage: Debug/Trace Headers
findings.remediation_brief: Strip all debug and trace headers from production responses. Review reverse proxy and application framework header emission configuration.
findings.description: Debug or trace response headers (e.g., X-Debug-Info, X-Request-Id with sensitive stack details, X-Trace) expose internal application state, timing, or infrastructure details that assist attackers.
findings._x_remediation: Strip all debug and trace headers from production responses. Review reverse proxy and application framework header emission configuration.

findings.title: Unknown Header Identified
findings.remediation_brief: Review all custom response headers and remove those that disclose internal implementation details.
findings.description: An unrecognised HTTP response header was identified. Custom or proprietary headers may disclose internal platform details, testing infrastructure, or undocumented API features.
findings._x_remediation: Review all custom response headers and remove those that disclose internal implementation details.

findings.title: Software Version Disclosed
findings.remediation_brief: Remove version disclosure from all response surfaces. Suppress generator tags, version comments, and version-bearing headers.
findings.description: Software version information was identified in response headers, HTML meta tags, error pages, or JavaScript files. A known version allows attackers to rapidly identify applicable CVEs.
findings._x_remediation: Remove version disclosure from all response surfaces. Suppress generator tags, version comments, and version-bearing headers.

findings.title: Virtual Host Discovered
findings.remediation_brief: Restrict virtual host binding to expected Host headers. Return consistent responses for unrecognised Host header values.
findings.description: A virtual host was identified via Host header fuzzing or DNS enumeration. Additional virtual hosts on the same IP may have weaker security configurations or expose internal applications.
findings._x_remediation: Restrict virtual host binding to expected Host headers. Return consistent responses for unrecognised Host header values.

findings.title: Subdomain Takeover — Dangling CNAME
findings.remediation_brief: Remove dangling CNAME records from DNS. Ensure external service accounts are active while DNS records reference them.
findings.description: A CNAME DNS record points to an unclaimed external service endpoint. An attacker can claim this endpoint and serve malicious content under the target's domain, enabling phishing, credential theft, and cookie theft.
findings._x_remediation: Remove dangling CNAME records from DNS. Ensure external service accounts are active while DNS records reference them.

findings.title: Subdomain Takeover Indicator
findings.remediation_brief: Verify whether the external service account has been deprovisioned. Remove the DNS record or re-claim the service endpoint.
findings.description: A response pattern suggesting a potential subdomain takeover was detected. The subdomain may be claimable on the identified external platform.
findings._x_remediation: Verify whether the external service account has been deprovisioned. Remove the DNS record or re-claim the service endpoint.

findings.title: DNS Zone Transfer Permitted (AXFR)
findings.remediation_brief: Restrict AXFR to authorised secondary DNS servers only. Configure ACLs on the DNS server to deny zone transfer requests from untrusted sources.
findings.description: The DNS server permits full zone transfer (AXFR) requests, allowing any external host to retrieve all DNS records for the domain. This exposes internal hostnames, IP addresses, and infrastructure topology.
findings._x_remediation: Restrict AXFR to authorised secondary DNS servers only. Configure ACLs on the DNS server to deny zone transfer requests from untrusted sources.

findings.title: Interesting Endpoint Discovered
findings.remediation_brief: Review discovered endpoints and ensure appropriate access controls are in place.
findings.description: An interesting URL or endpoint was discovered during crawling or discovery. The endpoint may expose sensitive functionality, administrative interfaces, or API capabilities.
findings._x_remediation: Review discovered endpoints and ensure appropriate access controls are in place.

findings.title: Authenticated Interesting Endpoint
findings.remediation_brief: Review the endpoint and apply least-privilege role-based access controls.
findings.description: An interesting endpoint was discovered while authenticated. The endpoint may expose functionality that should be restricted to specific roles only.
findings._x_remediation: Review the endpoint and apply least-privilege role-based access controls.

findings.title: Sensitive File Exposed
findings.remediation_brief: Remove or restrict access to sensitive files. Ensure web root contains only publicly accessible content.
findings.description: A sensitive file was found accessible on the web server. Sensitive files may contain credentials, configuration data, private keys, source code, or database contents.
findings._x_remediation: Remove or restrict access to sensitive files. Ensure web root contains only publicly accessible content.

findings.title: Sensitive Path Accessible
findings.remediation_brief: Apply authentication and authorisation controls to all sensitive paths. Implement a default-deny access policy.
findings.description: A sensitive path was found accessible that should require authentication or should not be publicly reachable. Accessing this path may expose administrative functionality, configuration, or credentials.
findings._x_remediation: Apply authentication and authorisation controls to all sensitive paths. Implement a default-deny access policy.

findings.title: Admin Panel Exposed
findings.remediation_brief: Restrict admin panel access by IP allowlist. Require multi-factor authentication for all administrative access. Do not expose admin interfaces to the public internet.
findings.description: An administrative panel or management interface was found publicly accessible. Exposure of admin panels increases the attack surface for brute-force, credential stuffing, and privilege escalation attacks.
findings._x_remediation: Restrict admin panel access by IP allowlist. Require multi-factor authentication for all administrative access. Do not expose admin interfaces to the public internet.

findings.title: Exposed Admin/Debug Endpoint
findings.remediation_brief: Remove debug endpoints from production deployments. Restrict access to any legitimate admin endpoints by IP allowlist and authentication.
findings.description: A debug or administrative endpoint was found publicly accessible. These endpoints may expose configuration data, heap dumps, environment variables, or allow remote code execution.
findings._x_remediation: Remove debug endpoints from production deployments. Restrict access to any legitimate admin endpoints by IP allowlist and authentication.

findings.title: Web Files Downloaded
findings.remediation_brief: Review all downloadable files and ensure they do not expose sensitive information. Remove backup files from web-accessible directories.
findings.description: Downloadable files (e.g., backups, exports, documents) were identified on the web server. Downloadable files may contain sensitive information including credentials, source code, or internal data.
findings._x_remediation: Review all downloadable files and ensure they do not expose sensitive information. Remove backup files from web-accessible directories.

findings.title: Web Screenshot Captured
findings.remediation_brief: No remediation required. Screenshots are captured for assessment documentation purposes.
findings.description: A screenshot of the web application was captured using a headless browser. This provides visual context for the application's UI, authentication flows, and security controls.
findings._x_remediation: No remediation required. Screenshots are captured for assessment documentation purposes.

findings.title: Hidden Parameter Discovered
findings.remediation_brief: Review hidden parameters and ensure they do not bypass security controls or expose sensitive functionality.
findings.description: A hidden form parameter or non-visible request parameter was discovered. Hidden parameters may be used to pass state or control values that are not exposed in the UI but are processed server-side.
findings._x_remediation: Review hidden parameters and ensure they do not bypass security controls or expose sensitive functionality.

findings.title: Non-Login Form Detected
findings.remediation_brief: Ensure all forms are protected against CSRF and injection. Apply input validation and output encoding.
findings.description: A non-authentication form was detected in the application. Forms may be entry points for injection attacks, CSRF, or data manipulation vulnerabilities.
findings._x_remediation: Ensure all forms are protected against CSRF and injection. Apply input validation and output encoding.

findings.title: Login Page Detected
findings.remediation_brief: Implement account lockout, rate limiting, CAPTCHA, and MFA on all login pages.
findings.description: An authentication login page was identified. The login page is the primary target for brute-force, credential stuffing, and authentication bypass attacks.
findings._x_remediation: Implement account lockout, rate limiting, CAPTCHA, and MFA on all login pages.

findings.title: Application Identified at Login Page
findings.remediation_brief: Suppress technology-identifying indicators from login pages.
findings.description: The application technology or platform was identified from the login page appearance, form fields, or response headers. This aids attacker reconnaissance of version-specific authentication vulnerabilities.
findings._x_remediation: Suppress technology-identifying indicators from login pages.

findings.title: Authentication Method Identified
findings.remediation_brief: Use strong, modern authentication mechanisms. Ensure credentials are transmitted only over encrypted channels.
findings.description: The authentication method used by the application was identified (e.g., form-based login, HTTP Basic, Digest, NTLM, Token, TOTP MFA). Understanding the auth method helps target appropriate attack vectors.
findings._x_remediation: Use strong, modern authentication mechanisms. Ensure credentials are transmitted only over encrypted channels.

findings.title: Password Reset Endpoint Exposed
findings.remediation_brief: Ensure password reset tokens are cryptographically random, single-use, and short-lived. Validate the Host header in reset link generation.
findings.description: A password reset endpoint was identified. Password reset flows are frequently targeted for account takeover via insecure token handling, predictable tokens, or host header injection.
findings._x_remediation: Ensure password reset tokens are cryptographically random, single-use, and short-lived. Validate the Host header in reset link generation.

findings.title: Active Session Management Interface Detected
findings.remediation_brief: Restrict session management interfaces to authenticated users with appropriate roles. Ensure session identifiers are not exposed in the UI.
findings.description: An active session management interface was detected (e.g., a page showing currently active sessions). This interface may expose session identifiers, user details, or allow unauthorised session termination.
findings._x_remediation: Restrict session management interfaces to authenticated users with appropriate roles. Ensure session identifiers are not exposed in the UI.

findings.title: File Upload Endpoint Detected
findings.remediation_brief: Validate file type by content inspection (not extension alone). Store uploads outside the web root. Disable execution of uploaded files. Implement file size limits and antivirus scanning.
findings.description: A file upload endpoint was detected. File upload functionality is a common attack vector for web shell upload, client-side XSS via crafted files, and server-side processing vulnerabilities.
findings._x_remediation: Validate file type by content inspection (not extension alone). Store uploads outside the web root. Disable execution of uploaded files. Implement file size limits and antivirus scanning.

findings.title: WordPress Version Detected
findings.remediation_brief: Remove version disclosure from generator meta tags and restrict access to files that reveal version information. Keep WordPress core updated to the latest stable release.
findings.description: The WordPress version was identified. A known version allows attackers to rapidly identify version-specific CVEs affecting WordPress core.
findings._x_remediation: Remove version disclosure from generator meta tags and restrict access to files that reveal version information. Keep WordPress core updated to the latest stable release.

findings.title: WordPress Vulnerability / Misconfiguration
findings.remediation_brief: Apply all available WordPress security patches. Review and harden WordPress security settings per the WordPress hardening guide.
findings.description: A WordPress-specific vulnerability or security misconfiguration was identified. WordPress misconfigurations may allow unauthenticated access, information disclosure, or remote code execution.
findings._x_remediation: Apply all available WordPress security patches. Review and harden WordPress security settings per the WordPress hardening guide.

findings.title: WordPress Users Exposed via REST API
findings.remediation_brief: Disable username exposure via the REST API by filtering the response or disabling the endpoint with appropriate plugins. Implement account lockout on wp-login.php.
findings.description: WordPress usernames were enumerated via the REST API /wp-json/wp/v2/users endpoint. Exposed usernames enable targeted brute-force and credential stuffing attacks against wp-login.php.
findings._x_remediation: Disable username exposure via the REST API by filtering the response or disabling the endpoint with appropriate plugins. Implement account lockout on wp-login.php.

findings.title: WordPress User Enumeration via Author Archives
findings.remediation_brief: Prevent author archive enumeration by redirecting /?author=N requests or using a security plugin to obfuscate author slugs.
findings.description: WordPress usernames were enumerated by probing author archive URLs (?author=N). The server redirected to user-specific author archive pages revealing valid usernames.
findings._x_remediation: Prevent author archive enumeration by redirecting /?author=N requests or using a security plugin to obfuscate author slugs.

findings.title: WordPress Debug Log Exposed
findings.remediation_brief: Disable WP_DEBUG and WP_DEBUG_LOG in production. Remove the debug.log file and restrict access to wp-content/ directory.
findings.description: The WordPress debug log (wp-content/debug.log) is publicly accessible. Debug logs may contain database credentials, file paths, error messages, and other sensitive internal information.
findings._x_remediation: Disable WP_DEBUG and WP_DEBUG_LOG in production. Remove the debug.log file and restrict access to wp-content/ directory.

findings.title: WordPress wp-config.php Source Code Exposed
findings.remediation_brief: Move wp-config.php one directory above the web root. Block access to backup files matching wp-config patterns via .htaccess or server configuration.
findings.description: The WordPress configuration file (wp-config.php) or a backup of it is accessible and returns source code. This file contains database credentials, authentication keys, and salts.
findings._x_remediation: Move wp-config.php one directory above the web root. Block access to backup files matching wp-config patterns via .htaccess or server configuration.

findings.title: WordPress wp-cron.php Publicly Accessible
findings.remediation_brief: Disable the default WP-Cron mechanism and replace it with a real server cron job. Block direct external access to wp-cron.php via web server configuration.
findings.description: The WordPress wp-cron.php file is publicly accessible and can be triggered by external requests. Unrestricted access allows attackers to trigger scheduled tasks at will, potentially causing resource exhaustion or unintended side effects.
findings._x_remediation: Disable the default WP-Cron mechanism and replace it with a real server cron job. Block direct external access to wp-cron.php via web server configuration.

findings.title: WordPress Multisite Installation Detected
findings.remediation_brief: Ensure all sites in the Multisite network are monitored and updated. Apply network-wide security controls.
findings.description: A WordPress Multisite installation was detected. Multisite installations have a larger attack surface as vulnerabilities in one site may affect all sites in the network.
findings._x_remediation: Ensure all sites in the Multisite network are monitored and updated. Apply network-wide security controls.

findings.title: WordPress Plugins Detected in Page Source
findings.remediation_brief: Dequeue unused plugins and obfuscate plugin asset paths where possible. Keep all plugins updated.
findings.description: WordPress plugin names were identified from page source references to wp-content/plugins/. Known plugin names allow attackers to check for plugin-specific CVEs.
findings._x_remediation: Dequeue unused plugins and obfuscate plugin asset paths where possible. Keep all plugins updated.

findings.title: WordPress Parent Theme Detected
findings.remediation_brief: Keep all themes updated. Remove unused themes.
findings.description: A WordPress parent theme was identified. Known theme names allow attackers to check for theme-specific CVEs and misconfigurations.
findings._x_remediation: Keep all themes updated. Remove unused themes.

findings.title: WordPress Backup/Export File Exposed
findings.remediation_brief: Remove backup files from web-accessible directories. Store backups outside the document root or with access restrictions.
findings.description: A WordPress backup or export file was found accessible on the web server. These files may contain the full database dump including user credentials, content, and configuration.
findings._x_remediation: Remove backup files from web-accessible directories. Store backups outside the document root or with access restrictions.

findings.title: WordPress Configuration Backup Exposed
findings.remediation_brief: Remove configuration backup files from web-accessible directories. Ensure backup files are stored securely outside the web root.
findings.description: A WordPress configuration backup file was found accessible. Configuration backups may expose database credentials, salts, and authentication keys.
findings._x_remediation: Remove configuration backup files from web-accessible directories. Ensure backup files are stored securely outside the web root.

findings.title: WordPress Directory Listing Enabled
findings.remediation_brief: Disable directory listing via the web server configuration. Add Options -Indexes to .htaccess or equivalent in nginx configuration.
findings.description: Directory listing is enabled on a WordPress directory (wp-content, plugins, themes, or uploads). This allows enumeration of installed plugins, themes, media files, and backup files.
findings._x_remediation: Disable directory listing via the web server configuration. Add Options -Indexes to .htaccess or equivalent in nginx configuration.

findings.title: PHP Error Log Exposed
findings.remediation_brief: Configure PHP to log errors to a file outside the web root. Restrict web server access to log files.
findings.description: A PHP error log file is publicly accessible. Error logs may contain database credentials, file system paths, internal function names, SQL queries, and stack traces.
findings._x_remediation: Configure PHP to log errors to a file outside the web root. Restrict web server access to log files.

findings.title: TimThumb Script Detected
findings.remediation_brief: Remove TimThumb from the application. If required, update to the latest version (2.8.14+) and restrict the allowed domain list.
findings.description: The TimThumb image resizing script was detected. Outdated versions of TimThumb contain remote file inclusion vulnerabilities that allow attackers to download and execute remote PHP code.
findings._x_remediation: Remove TimThumb from the application. If required, update to the latest version (2.8.14+) and restrict the allowed domain list.

findings.title: Sensitive WordPress Path Accessible
findings.remediation_brief: Restrict access to all sensitive WordPress paths via web server configuration. Review WordPress hardening guidelines.
findings.description: A sensitive WordPress file or directory was found publicly accessible. This may expose credentials, configuration, or internal application data.
findings._x_remediation: Restrict access to all sensitive WordPress paths via web server configuration. Review WordPress hardening guidelines.

findings.title: SSL/TLS Certificate Information
findings.remediation_brief: Ensure certificate expiry is monitored with automated renewal. Verify all expected FQDNs are listed in the SAN extension.
findings.description: TLS certificate identity and validity metadata was extracted including subject CN, issuer, Subject Alternative Names (SANs), and expiry date. This provides reference context for the certificate lifecycle and scope.
findings._x_remediation: Ensure certificate expiry is monitored with automated renewal. Verify all expected FQDNs are listed in the SAN extension.

findings.title: SSL/TLS Certificate: Expired
findings.remediation_brief: Renew the certificate immediately and implement automated renewal (e.g., ACME/Let's Encrypt) to prevent future expiry.
findings.description: The server's TLS certificate has passed its expiry date, causing browser trust errors and indicating a breakdown in certificate lifecycle management.
findings._x_remediation: Renew the certificate immediately and implement automated renewal (e.g., ACME/Let's Encrypt) to prevent future expiry.

findings.title: SSL/TLS Certificate: Hostname Mismatch
findings.remediation_brief: Reissue the certificate to include the target hostname in the Subject Alternative Name extension.
findings.description: The TLS certificate's Subject Alternative Names do not cover the target hostname. Clients will display a certificate mismatch warning, enabling trivial MITM attacks.
findings._x_remediation: Reissue the certificate to include the target hostname in the Subject Alternative Name extension.

findings.title: SSL/TLS Certificate: Self-Signed
findings.remediation_brief: Replace self-signed certificates with certificates issued by a trusted CA. Use ACME/Let's Encrypt for automated issuance.
findings.description: The server presented a self-signed TLS certificate not anchored to a publicly trusted CA, preventing clients from verifying the server's identity and enabling trivial MITM attacks.
findings._x_remediation: Replace self-signed certificates with certificates issued by a trusted CA. Use ACME/Let's Encrypt for automated issuance.

findings.title: SSL/TLS DNS: Missing CAA Record
findings.remediation_brief: Add a CAA record specifying the authorised CA(s) for certificate issuance.
findings.description: No CAA (Certification Authority Authorization) DNS record exists for the domain. Without CAA, any certificate authority can issue certificates for this domain, increasing mis-issuance risk.
findings._x_remediation: Add a CAA record specifying the authorised CA(s) for certificate issuance.

findings.title: SSL/TLS Vulnerability: SWEET32
findings.remediation_brief: Disable all 3DES cipher suites. Use AEAD ciphers (AES-GCM) only.
findings.description: 3DES cipher suites are accepted, making the server susceptible to the SWEET32 birthday attack (CVE-2016-2183). An attacker can recover plaintext from long-lived sessions using 3DES by collecting enough ciphertext blocks.
findings._x_remediation: Disable all 3DES cipher suites. Use AEAD ciphers (AES-GCM) only.

findings.title: SSL/TLS Vulnerability: BEAST
findings.remediation_brief: Disable TLSv1.0 and CBC cipher suites. Use TLS 1.2/1.3 with AEAD ciphers only.
findings.description: TLSv1.0 is enabled with CBC cipher suites, making the server susceptible to the BEAST attack (CVE-2011-3389). BEAST allows an active MITM to partially decrypt TLS-encrypted session data.
findings._x_remediation: Disable TLSv1.0 and CBC cipher suites. Use TLS 1.2/1.3 with AEAD ciphers only.

findings.title: SSL/TLS Vulnerability: LUCKY13
findings.remediation_brief: Prefer AEAD cipher suites (AES-GCM/AES-CCM) over CBC-mode ciphers.
findings.description: CBC cipher suites are accepted, making the server susceptible to the LUCKY13 timing attack (CVE-2013-0169). LUCKY13 allows an attacker to recover plaintext from CBC-mode TLS using timing side-channels.
findings._x_remediation: Prefer AEAD cipher suites (AES-GCM/AES-CCM) over CBC-mode ciphers.

findings.title: TLS Version Identified
findings.remediation_brief: Ensure TLS 1.2 or 1.3 is negotiated. Disable TLS 1.0 and 1.1.
findings.description: The negotiated TLS protocol version was identified via a socket-level probe. This provides baseline TLS version context when sslscan/testssl.sh are unavailable.
findings._x_remediation: Ensure TLS 1.2 or 1.3 is negotiated. Disable TLS 1.0 and 1.1.

findings.title: Weak Cipher Identified
findings.remediation_brief: Disable all weak cipher suites. Use only AEAD ciphers (AES-128-GCM, AES-256-GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305). Enable TLS 1.3 only for new deployments.
findings.description: A weak or deprecated cipher suite was identified in the server's TLS configuration. Weak ciphers may allow passive decryption of TLS traffic by a well-resourced attacker.
findings._x_remediation: Disable all weak cipher suites. Use only AEAD ciphers (AES-128-GCM, AES-256-GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305). Enable TLS 1.3 only for new deployments.

findings.title: Heartbleed (CVE-2014-0160) Vulnerability Detected
findings.remediation_brief: Update OpenSSL to 1.0.1g+ or 1.0.2+. Revoke and reissue all certificates. Invalidate all active session tokens.
findings.description: The server is vulnerable to Heartbleed (CVE-2014-0160). Attackers can read up to 64 KB of server memory per request, exposing private keys, session tokens, and credentials without authentication.
findings._x_remediation: Update OpenSSL to 1.0.1g+ or 1.0.2+. Revoke and reissue all certificates. Invalidate all active session tokens.

findings.title: SSL/TLS Grade
findings.remediation_brief: Remediate identified TLS weaknesses to achieve a grade of A or better.
findings.description: testssl.sh assigned an overall TLS grade to the target. The grade summarises the TLS configuration quality across protocol versions, cipher suites, and certificate strength.
findings._x_remediation: Remediate identified TLS weaknesses to achieve a grade of A or better.

findings.title: Missing Security Header
findings.remediation_brief: Configure all recommended security headers: Content-Security-Policy, Strict-Transport-Security, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy.
findings.description: One or more HTTP security headers are absent from the server response. Missing security headers weaken the browser's ability to enforce content security policies, prevent clickjacking, and mitigate XSS.
findings._x_remediation: Configure all recommended security headers: Content-Security-Policy, Strict-Transport-Security, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy.

findings.title: Permissive Security Header: Content-Security-Policy
findings.remediation_brief: Replace permissive CSP directives with specific, trusted origins. Use nonces or hashes instead of 'unsafe-inline'.
findings.description: The Content-Security-Policy header is present but contains permissive directives such as 'unsafe-inline', 'unsafe-eval', or wildcard ('*') sources that significantly weaken its XSS protection.
findings._x_remediation: Replace permissive CSP directives with specific, trusted origins. Use nonces or hashes instead of 'unsafe-inline'.

findings.title: Permissive Security Header: X-Frame-Options
findings.remediation_brief: Set X-Frame-Options to DENY or SAMEORIGIN. Prefer the frame-ancestors CSP directive for modern browsers.
findings.description: The X-Frame-Options header is set to ALLOW-FROM or is absent, allowing the page to be embedded in iframes from arbitrary origins and enabling clickjacking attacks.
findings._x_remediation: Set X-Frame-Options to DENY or SAMEORIGIN. Prefer the frame-ancestors CSP directive for modern browsers.

findings.title: Permissive Security Header: Strict-Transport-Security
findings.remediation_brief: Set HSTS max-age to at least 31536000 (1 year) and include the includeSubDomains directive. Consider adding to the HSTS preload list.
findings.description: The Strict-Transport-Security header is present but has an insufficient max-age value or is missing the includeSubDomains directive.
findings._x_remediation: Set HSTS max-age to at least 31536000 (1 year) and include the includeSubDomains directive. Consider adding to the HSTS preload list.

findings.title: Permissive Security Header: Referrer-Policy
findings.remediation_brief: Set Referrer-Policy to 'strict-origin-when-cross-origin' or 'no-referrer'.
findings.description: The Referrer-Policy header allows sensitive URL information to be included in the Referer header sent to third-party origins, potentially leaking authentication tokens or PII.
findings._x_remediation: Set Referrer-Policy to 'strict-origin-when-cross-origin' or 'no-referrer'.

findings.title: Permissive Security Header: X-Content-Type-Options
findings.remediation_brief: Set X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff on all responses.
findings.description: The X-Content-Type-Options header is missing or set to a value other than 'nosniff', allowing browsers to MIME-sniff the content type and execute uploaded files as scripts.
findings._x_remediation: Set X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff on all responses.

findings.title: Permissive Security Header: Cache-Control
findings.remediation_brief: Set 'Cache-Control: no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate' on all authenticated and sensitive pages.
findings.description: Sensitive pages lack appropriate Cache-Control directives, allowing browser or proxy caches to store sensitive data. Cached sensitive pages may be retrieved by other users of shared devices.
findings._x_remediation: Set 'Cache-Control: no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate' on all authenticated and sensitive pages.

findings.title: Missing Cache-Control on Sensitive Page
findings.remediation_brief: Add 'Cache-Control: no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate' to all pages that display authenticated or sensitive data.
