findings.description: An authenticated or sensitive page does not set Cache-Control headers to prevent caching. The page content may be stored in browser or proxy caches and retrieved by subsequent users.
findings._x_remediation: Add 'Cache-Control: no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate' to all pages that display authenticated or sensitive data.

findings.title: Misconfigured Expect-CT Header (max-age=0 with enforce)
findings.remediation_brief: Remove the enforce directive or set an appropriate max-age value for Expect-CT. Consider relying on the browser's built-in CT enforcement instead.
findings.description: The Expect-CT header is set with max-age=0 and the enforce directive. This configuration is contradictory and ineffective for certificate transparency enforcement.
findings._x_remediation: Remove the enforce directive or set an appropriate max-age value for Expect-CT. Consider relying on the browser's built-in CT enforcement instead.

findings.title: Endpoint-Specific Security Header Found
findings.remediation_brief: Ensure security headers are applied consistently across all application endpoints via server-level configuration rather than per-page.
findings.description: A security header was found present on a specific endpoint but absent on the main application root. Inconsistent header coverage may leave some pages vulnerable despite partial protection.
findings._x_remediation: Ensure security headers are applied consistently across all application endpoints via server-level configuration rather than per-page.

findings.title: SQL Injection (Error-Based)
findings.remediation_brief: Use parameterised queries or prepared statements. Never construct SQL queries from user input. Suppress detailed database error messages in production.
findings.description: Error-based SQL injection was detected. Database error messages containing SQL syntax are returned in response to crafted input, confirming the application is vulnerable to SQL injection and disclosing database version/structure information.
findings._x_remediation: Use parameterised queries or prepared statements. Never construct SQL queries from user input. Suppress detailed database error messages in production.

findings.title: SQL Injection Confirmed by sqlmap
findings.remediation_brief: Use parameterised queries or prepared statements. Apply input validation. Restrict database account permissions to the minimum required.
findings.description: sqlmap confirmed SQL injection on the target parameter. SQL injection allows attackers to read, modify, or delete database contents and may enable operating system command execution.
findings._x_remediation: Use parameterised queries or prepared statements. Apply input validation. Restrict database account permissions to the minimum required.

findings.title: Second-Order SQL Injection
findings.remediation_brief: Apply parameterised queries at all database interaction points, not just at the input entry point. Sanitise data on retrieval as well as input.
findings.description: A second-order (stored) SQL injection vector was identified. User-supplied input stored in the database is later included in SQL queries without sanitisation when retrieved and processed.
findings._x_remediation: Apply parameterised queries at all database interaction points, not just at the input entry point. Sanitise data on retrieval as well as input.

findings.title: OS Command Injection
findings.remediation_brief: Never pass user input to shell functions. Use language-native APIs instead of shell commands. If shell commands are required, use allowlisted inputs only with strict sanitisation.
findings.description: OS command injection was detected. User-supplied input is passed to an operating system shell without sanitisation, allowing arbitrary command execution on the server.
findings._x_remediation: Never pass user input to shell functions. Use language-native APIs instead of shell commands. If shell commands are required, use allowlisted inputs only with strict sanitisation.

findings.title: Remote Code Execution via Code Injection
findings.remediation_brief: Never evaluate user-supplied input as code. Use a template engine that auto-escapes by default. Sanitise and validate all user input.
findings.description: Server-side code injection leading to remote code execution was detected. User-supplied input is evaluated as server-side code (PHP, Python, Ruby, etc.), allowing arbitrary code execution.
findings._x_remediation: Never evaluate user-supplied input as code. Use a template engine that auto-escapes by default. Sanitise and validate all user input.

findings.title: Reflected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
findings.remediation_brief: Apply context-sensitive output encoding for all user-controlled data. Implement a Content-Security-Policy header to restrict script execution.
findings.description: Reflected XSS was detected. User-supplied input is immediately reflected in the server response without encoding, allowing attackers to inject and execute arbitrary JavaScript in the victim's browser via a crafted link.
findings._x_remediation: Apply context-sensitive output encoding for all user-controlled data. Implement a Content-Security-Policy header to restrict script execution.

findings.title: Stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
findings.remediation_brief: Apply context-sensitive output encoding at render time. Implement Content-Security-Policy. Validate and sanitise all input before storage.
findings.description: Stored XSS was detected. User-supplied input is persisted and later rendered in the browser without encoding, allowing an attacker to execute JavaScript in the context of any user who views the affected page.
findings._x_remediation: Apply context-sensitive output encoding at render time. Implement Content-Security-Policy. Validate and sanitise all input before storage.

findings.title: DOM-Based Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
findings.remediation_brief: Avoid writing attacker-controllable data to dangerous DOM sinks (innerHTML, document.write, eval). Use textContent or safe DOM APIs. Apply a strict Content-Security-Policy.
findings.description: DOM-based XSS was detected. JavaScript in the page reads attacker-controlled data from an insecure source (URL fragment, query string, postMessage) and writes it to a dangerous sink without encoding.
findings._x_remediation: Avoid writing attacker-controllable data to dangerous DOM sinks (innerHTML, document.write, eval). Use textContent or safe DOM APIs. Apply a strict Content-Security-Policy.

findings.title: XSS Confirmed by dalfox
findings.remediation_brief: Apply context-sensitive output encoding. Implement a strict Content-Security-Policy. Validate and sanitise all user-supplied input.
findings.description: dalfox confirmed a Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability with a working payload that executes in the browser. XSS enables session hijacking, credential theft, and UI redirection.
findings._x_remediation: Apply context-sensitive output encoding. Implement a strict Content-Security-Policy. Validate and sanitise all user-supplied input.

findings.title: CSV / Formula Injection
findings.remediation_brief: Prefix cell values containing formula characters with a single quote or sanitise them before CSV export. Warn users about opening untrusted CSV files.
findings.description: CSV/formula injection was detected. User-supplied input containing spreadsheet formula characters (=, +, -, @) is included in CSV exports without sanitisation and may execute in spreadsheet applications opened by staff.
findings._x_remediation: Prefix cell values containing formula characters with a single quote or sanitise them before CSV export. Warn users about opening untrusted CSV files.

findings.title: CRLF Injection
findings.remediation_brief: Strip CRLF characters from all user input used in HTTP header values. Apply output encoding at HTTP header construction points.
findings.description: CRLF injection was detected. Carriage return and line feed characters in user input are reflected in HTTP response headers, allowing attackers to inject arbitrary headers or split responses.
findings._x_remediation: Strip CRLF characters from all user input used in HTTP header values. Apply output encoding at HTTP header construction points.

findings.title: Log Injection / CRLF in Log Entries
findings.remediation_brief: Sanitise all user input included in log messages. Remove or encode CRLF characters before logging.
findings.description: Log injection was detected. User-supplied input containing CRLF characters is written to application logs without sanitisation, allowing attackers to forge log entries and cover their tracks.
findings._x_remediation: Sanitise all user input included in log messages. Remove or encode CRLF characters before logging.

findings.title: HTTP Parameter Pollution (HPP)
findings.remediation_brief: Consistently parse HTTP parameters and reject or handle duplicate parameter names explicitly. Ensure security controls operate on the same parameter value the application uses.
findings.description: HTTP Parameter Pollution was detected. Duplicate query or body parameters with different values are processed inconsistently, potentially bypassing input validation or authentication checks.
findings._x_remediation: Consistently parse HTTP parameters and reject or handle duplicate parameter names explicitly. Ensure security controls operate on the same parameter value the application uses.

findings.title: HTTP Method Tampering
findings.remediation_brief: Restrict accepted HTTP methods to those explicitly required by the application. Return 405 Method Not Allowed for all other methods.
findings.description: An unexpected HTTP method was accepted by the server. Accepting non-standard methods (e.g., TRACE, PUT, DELETE, PATCH) may bypass WAF rules or expose administrative functionality.
findings._x_remediation: Restrict accepted HTTP methods to those explicitly required by the application. Return 405 Method Not Allowed for all other methods.

findings.title: HTTP TRACE Method Enabled (Cross-Site Tracing)
findings.remediation_brief: Disable the HTTP TRACE method in the web server configuration (TraceEnable Off in Apache; disabling in nginx).
findings.description: The HTTP TRACE method is enabled. TRACE echoes the full request including HTTP headers back to the client, enabling Cross-Site Tracing (XST) attacks that may expose HttpOnly cookies via XSS.
findings._x_remediation: Disable the HTTP TRACE method in the web server configuration (TraceEnable Off in Apache; disabling in nginx).

findings.title: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
findings.remediation_brief: Validate and allowlist all server-side request targets. Block requests to private IP ranges and cloud metadata endpoints. Use a dedicated outbound request proxy with allowlisting.
findings.description: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) was detected. User-supplied URLs or hostnames are used by the server to make outbound requests without validation, allowing attackers to probe internal services, bypass firewall rules, and access cloud metadata endpoints.
findings._x_remediation: Validate and allowlist all server-side request targets. Block requests to private IP ranges and cloud metadata endpoints. Use a dedicated outbound request proxy with allowlisting.

findings.title: Blind SSRF — Internal Network Probing
findings.remediation_brief: Validate and allowlist all server-side request targets. Use an SSRF-safe HTTP client library that blocks private IP ranges by default.
findings.description: Blind SSRF was detected via out-of-band interaction. The server made a DNS or HTTP request to an attacker-controlled host, confirming that user-supplied URLs trigger server-side requests. Internal network probing may be possible.
findings._x_remediation: Validate and allowlist all server-side request targets. Use an SSRF-safe HTTP client library that blocks private IP ranges by default.

findings.title: Insecure Deserialization — Serialized Object Accepted
findings.remediation_brief: Avoid deserialising objects from untrusted sources. If required, sign serialised data and verify signatures before deserialisation. Use safer serialisation formats (JSON) where possible.
findings.description: A serialised object was accepted by the application without signature verification. Insecure deserialisation can lead to remote code execution, privilege escalation, or denial of service depending on the deserialisable gadget chains available.
findings._x_remediation: Avoid deserialising objects from untrusted sources. If required, sign serialised data and verify signatures before deserialisation. Use safer serialisation formats (JSON) where possible.

findings.title: Insecure Deserialization — YAML Tag Injection
findings.remediation_brief: Use safe YAML loaders (yaml.safe_load in Python). Disable arbitrary Python object instantiation in the YAML parser.
findings.description: A YAML tag injection payload was accepted by the application. YAML parsers that support arbitrary Python object instantiation via !! tags (e.g., PyYAML) can be exploited for remote code execution.
findings._x_remediation: Use safe YAML loaders (yaml.safe_load in Python). Disable arbitrary Python object instantiation in the YAML parser.

findings.title: Insecure Deserialization — Error Disclosure
findings.remediation_brief: Suppress deserialisation errors in production. Apply the remediation for insecure deserialisation.
findings.description: A deserialisation error was triggered by a crafted payload and the error message was returned in the response. Error disclosure confirms the parameter is processed by a deserialiser and may guide further exploitation.
findings._x_remediation: Suppress deserialisation errors in production. Apply the remediation for insecure deserialisation.

findings.title: Verbose Error Messages — Stack Trace Disclosed
findings.remediation_brief: Configure the application to return generic error pages in production. Log detailed errors server-side only.
findings.description: A detailed stack trace or internal error message was returned in response to a crafted request. Stack traces disclose source file paths, class names, function names, and line numbers that assist further exploitation.
findings._x_remediation: Configure the application to return generic error pages in production. Log detailed errors server-side only.

findings.title: Credentials/Secret in JavaScript
findings.remediation_brief: Move all credentials and API keys to server-side configuration. Use environment variables and secret management solutions. Rotate any exposed credentials immediately.
findings.description: Credentials, API keys, tokens, or other secrets were identified in client-side JavaScript source files. Client-side secrets are visible to all users and attackers who access the page.
findings._x_remediation: Move all credentials and API keys to server-side configuration. Use environment variables and secret management solutions. Rotate any exposed credentials immediately.

findings.title: Sensitive Information in Source
findings.remediation_brief: Remove all sensitive data from page source. Use server-side rendering to avoid embedding sensitive values in HTML. Conduct regular source code reviews.
findings.description: Sensitive information (credentials, internal URLs, private keys, PII, or internal comments) was identified in the HTML source of the page.
findings._x_remediation: Remove all sensitive data from page source. Use server-side rendering to avoid embedding sensitive values in HTML. Conduct regular source code reviews.

findings.title: Weak or Default Credentials Accepted
findings.remediation_brief: Change all default credentials immediately. Enforce a strong password policy. Implement MFA. Conduct periodic credential audits.
findings.description: Weak, default, or commonly-used credentials were successfully authenticated. Default or weak credentials allow attackers to gain privileged access without effort.
findings._x_remediation: Change all default credentials immediately. Enforce a strong password policy. Implement MFA. Conduct periodic credential audits.

findings.title: Missing Rate Limiting / Brute-Force Protection
findings.remediation_brief: Implement progressive account lockout, CAPTCHA after failed attempts, and IP-based rate limiting on the login endpoint.
findings.description: The authentication endpoint does not implement rate limiting or brute-force protection. Attackers can submit unlimited login attempts to perform credential stuffing or password brute-forcing.
findings._x_remediation: Implement progressive account lockout, CAPTCHA after failed attempts, and IP-based rate limiting on the login endpoint.

findings.title: Insufficient Auth Failure Logging / No Brute-Force Detection
findings.remediation_brief: Log all authentication failures with timestamp, source IP, and username. Configure alerts for repeated failures from a single IP. Integrate with a SIEM for real-time detection.
findings.description: Authentication failures are not logged or no alerting is configured for repeated failures. Without logging, brute-force attacks may go undetected until after a successful compromise.
findings._x_remediation: Log all authentication failures with timestamp, source IP, and username. Configure alerts for repeated failures from a single IP. Integrate with a SIEM for real-time detection.

findings.title: Timing Attack — Non-Constant-Time Authentication
findings.remediation_brief: Use constant-time comparison functions for all credential verification. Ensure responses are returned after a fixed delay regardless of outcome.
findings.description: A statistically significant timing difference was observed between valid and invalid authentication attempts. Timing oracle attacks allow attackers to enumerate valid usernames or infer partial credential validity.
findings._x_remediation: Use constant-time comparison functions for all credential verification. Ensure responses are returned after a fixed delay regardless of outcome.

findings.title: JWT None Algorithm Authentication Bypass
findings.remediation_brief: Explicitly allowlist accepted JWT algorithms. Reject tokens with 'none' algorithm. Use a well-maintained JWT library with secure defaults.
findings.description: The JWT library accepts tokens with the 'none' algorithm, meaning the signature field is empty and no verification is performed. Attackers can forge arbitrary JWT payloads to impersonate any user including administrators.
findings._x_remediation: Explicitly allowlist accepted JWT algorithms. Reject tokens with 'none' algorithm. Use a well-maintained JWT library with secure defaults.

findings.title: JWT Vulnerability: 'none' Algorithm Accepted
findings.remediation_brief: Reject all tokens with 'none' algorithm. Explicitly specify and enforce the expected signature algorithm server-side.
findings.description: The application accepted a JWT token with the 'none' algorithm specified in the header, bypassing signature verification. This allows forging of arbitrary JWT claims.
findings._x_remediation: Reject all tokens with 'none' algorithm. Explicitly specify and enforce the expected signature algorithm server-side.

findings.title: JWT Vulnerability Confirmed by jwt_tool
findings.remediation_brief: Implement strict JWT validation: verify the signature algorithm, reject 'none' algorithm, validate all claims (exp, aud, iss). Rotate signing keys.
findings.description: jwt_tool confirmed a JWT vulnerability that allows token forgery or authentication bypass. JWT vulnerabilities enable impersonation of arbitrary users including administrators.
findings._x_remediation: Implement strict JWT validation: verify the signature algorithm, reject 'none' algorithm, validate all claims (exp, aud, iss). Rotate signing keys.

findings.title: JWT — Missing Expiry Claim (No exp)
findings.remediation_brief: Include an 'exp' claim in all JWTs. Set a short token lifetime appropriate for the use case. Implement token refresh flows.
findings.description: The JWT token does not contain an 'exp' (expiry) claim. Tokens without expiry never become invalid, meaning a stolen token grants permanent access until the signing key is rotated.
findings._x_remediation: Include an 'exp' claim in all JWTs. Set a short token lifetime appropriate for the use case. Implement token refresh flows.

findings.title: JWT Token Identified: Algorithm
findings.remediation_brief: Ensure JWT tokens are signed with a strong algorithm (RS256, ES256, or HS256 with a sufficiently random secret). Avoid 'none' or weak algorithms.
findings.description: A JWT token was identified in the application. The JWT header algorithm has been extracted for analysis.
findings._x_remediation: Ensure JWT tokens are signed with a strong algorithm (RS256, ES256, or HS256 with a sufficiently random secret). Avoid 'none' or weak algorithms.

findings.title: Potentially Predictable Session Token
findings.remediation_brief: Use a cryptographically secure random number generator for session token generation. Tokens must have at least 128 bits of entropy.
findings.description: The session token appears to have low entropy or a predictable pattern. Predictable tokens allow attackers to brute-force or enumerate valid sessions and impersonate other users.
findings._x_remediation: Use a cryptographically secure random number generator for session token generation. Tokens must have at least 128 bits of entropy.

findings.title: Low-Entropy Session Token
findings.remediation_brief: Generate session tokens using a CSPRNG. Ensure tokens have at least 128 bits of randomness.
findings.description: The session token has low statistical entropy as measured across multiple sample tokens. Low-entropy tokens can be brute-forced to hijack arbitrary user sessions.
findings._x_remediation: Generate session tokens using a CSPRNG. Ensure tokens have at least 128 bits of randomness.

findings.title: Session Fixation Vulnerability
findings.remediation_brief: Regenerate the session identifier immediately after every successful login. Invalidate the pre-authentication session ID.
findings.description: The application does not rotate the session identifier after successful authentication. An attacker can set a known session ID, trick the victim into authenticating, and then use the known ID to hijack the authenticated session.
findings._x_remediation: Regenerate the session identifier immediately after every successful login. Invalidate the pre-authentication session ID.

findings.title: Session Not Invalidated After Logout
findings.remediation_brief: Invalidate server-side session state on logout. Expire the session cookie immediately on the client. Do not rely solely on client-side cookie deletion.
findings.description: The server-side session is not invalidated after the user logs out. The session token remains valid for an extended period after logout, allowing session reuse if the token is captured.
findings._x_remediation: Invalidate server-side session state on logout. Expire the session cookie immediately on the client. Do not rely solely on client-side cookie deletion.

findings.title: Session Not Invalidated Server-Side After Logout
findings.remediation_brief: Implement server-side session invalidation on logout. Maintain a server-side session store that immediately marks tokens as invalid on logout.
findings.description: The pre-logout session token remains valid server-side after the logout request. An attacker who obtains a session token can continue to use it indefinitely after the legitimate user has logged out.
findings._x_remediation: Implement server-side session invalidation on logout. Maintain a server-side session store that immediately marks tokens as invalid on logout.

findings.title: Session Timeout Absent or Excessive
findings.remediation_brief: Implement server-side session timeout. Expire idle sessions after 15-30 minutes for sensitive applications. Set appropriate cookie Max-Age/Expires attributes.
findings.description: The session does not expire after a reasonable period of inactivity, or no session timeout is configured. Long-lived sessions increase the window of opportunity for session hijacking attacks.
findings._x_remediation: Implement server-side session timeout. Expire idle sessions after 15-30 minutes for sensitive applications. Set appropriate cookie Max-Age/Expires attributes.

findings.title: Excessive Session Timeout Configured
findings.remediation_brief: Set session lifetimes appropriate to the application sensitivity. Use refresh token patterns for long-lived access.
findings.description: The session cookie or JWT has an excessive lifetime (e.g., multiple days or weeks) that does not reflect the risk level of the application. Long-lived tokens extend the exposure window after theft.
findings._x_remediation: Set session lifetimes appropriate to the application sensitivity. Use refresh token patterns for long-lived access.

findings.title: Session Cookie SameSite=None Without Secure Flag
findings.remediation_brief: Always set the Secure flag alongside SameSite=None. Enforce HTTPS for all endpoints that issue cookies.
findings.description: A session cookie is set with SameSite=None but without the Secure flag. Without Secure, the cookie is transmitted over plaintext HTTP when SameSite=None is used, enabling cross-site transmission of session tokens.
findings._x_remediation: Always set the Secure flag alongside SameSite=None. Enforce HTTPS for all endpoints that issue cookies.

findings.title: Missing Secure Cookie Attribute: Secure
findings.remediation_brief: Set the Secure flag on all cookies. Enforce HTTPS site-wide.
findings.description: A non-session cookie lacks the Secure attribute. Without Secure, the cookie is transmitted over unencrypted HTTP connections.
findings._x_remediation: Set the Secure flag on all cookies. Enforce HTTPS site-wide.

findings.title: Missing Secure Cookie Attribute: HttpOnly
findings.remediation_brief: Set the HttpOnly flag on all cookies that do not require JavaScript access.
findings.description: A non-session cookie lacks the HttpOnly attribute. Without HttpOnly, client-side JavaScript can read the cookie value, enabling theft via XSS.
findings._x_remediation: Set the HttpOnly flag on all cookies that do not require JavaScript access.

findings.title: Missing Secure Cookie Attribute: SameSite
findings.remediation_brief: Set SameSite=Strict or SameSite=Lax on all cookies. Use SameSite=None only when cross-site sharing is required (and always with Secure).
findings.description: A cookie lacks the SameSite attribute. Without SameSite, the cookie is sent with cross-site requests, enabling CSRF attacks.
findings._x_remediation: Set SameSite=Strict or SameSite=Lax on all cookies. Use SameSite=None only when cross-site sharing is required (and always with Secure).

findings.title: Misconfigured Secure Cookie Attribute: SameSite
findings.remediation_brief: Audit all cookie SameSite configurations. Set SameSite=Strict where possible and always pair SameSite=None with Secure.
findings.description: A cookie has a misconfigured SameSite attribute (e.g., SameSite=None without Secure). Misconfigured SameSite settings can negate CSRF protections or expose cookies over plaintext HTTP.
findings._x_remediation: Audit all cookie SameSite configurations. Set SameSite=Strict where possible and always pair SameSite=None with Secure.

findings.title: No Logout (Logoff) Function Detected
findings.remediation_brief: Implement a logout endpoint that invalidates the server-side session and clears session cookies. Make the logout function visible and accessible from all authenticated pages.
findings.description: No logout or logoff function was identified in the application. Without an explicit logout mechanism, users cannot terminate their sessions, and sessions remain active until they expire naturally.
findings._x_remediation: Implement a logout endpoint that invalidates the server-side session and clears session cookies. Make the logout function visible and accessible from all authenticated pages.

findings.title: No Concurrent Session Limit Detected
findings.remediation_brief: Implement a concurrent session limit appropriate to the application's risk profile. Alert users when new sessions are established from new locations.
findings.description: The application allows unlimited concurrent sessions for a single user account. Without a concurrent session limit, compromised credentials can be exploited from multiple locations simultaneously without detection.
findings._x_remediation: Implement a concurrent session limit appropriate to the application's risk profile. Alert users when new sessions are established from new locations.

findings.title: Concurrent Session Limit Enforced
findings.remediation_brief: No remediation required. This is a positive security control.
findings.description: The application enforces a concurrent session limit. When a new session is established, existing sessions are invalidated. This limits the damage from compromised credentials.
findings._x_remediation: No remediation required. This is a positive security control.

findings.title: CORS Misconfiguration Allowing Credential Leakage
findings.remediation_brief: Do not reflect arbitrary origins in Access-Control-Allow-Origin when credentials are enabled. Maintain an explicit allowlist of trusted origins.
findings.description: The CORS configuration reflects arbitrary origins with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true. This allows attacker-controlled websites to make credentialed cross-origin requests and read the response, enabling session hijacking and sensitive data theft.
findings._x_remediation: Do not reflect arbitrary origins in Access-Control-Allow-Origin when credentials are enabled. Maintain an explicit allowlist of trusted origins.

findings.title: JSONP Endpoint — Cross-Origin Data Leakage
findings.remediation_brief: Replace JSONP with CORS. If JSONP must be retained, validate the callback parameter against a strict allowlist and enforce authentication.
findings.description: A JSONP endpoint was identified. JSONP endpoints allow any website to read the response content by including a script tag, bypassing the Same-Origin Policy and enabling cross-origin data exfiltration.
findings._x_remediation: Replace JSONP with CORS. If JSONP must be retained, validate the callback parameter against a strict allowlist and enforce authentication.

findings.title: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) — Missing Token
findings.remediation_brief: Implement CSRF protection using synchroniser tokens, double-submit cookies, or SameSite=Strict/Lax cookies. Verify the Origin or Referer header for same-site enforcement.
findings.description: A state-changing request (POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE) does not include a CSRF token or other origin verification mechanism. Attackers can trick authenticated users into making unintended requests from any website.
findings._x_remediation: Implement CSRF protection using synchroniser tokens, double-submit cookies, or SameSite=Strict/Lax cookies. Verify the Origin or Referer header for same-site enforcement.

findings.title: Unauthenticated Access to Protected Path
findings.remediation_brief: Apply authentication middleware to all protected routes. Adopt a default-deny access policy.
findings.description: A path or endpoint that should require authentication returned a successful response (HTTP 200) without providing valid credentials. This allows unauthenticated users to access protected functionality or data.
findings._x_remediation: Apply authentication middleware to all protected routes. Adopt a default-deny access policy.

findings.title: Debug Mode Enabled / Developer Console Exposed
findings.remediation_brief: Disable debug mode in production. Remove all debug endpoints and developer consoles from production deployments.
findings.description: A debug mode or developer console is enabled and publicly accessible. Debug interfaces may expose command execution, environment variables, stack traces, and database query information.
findings._x_remediation: Disable debug mode in production. Remove all debug endpoints and developer consoles from production deployments.

findings.title: Cross-User Data Leakage (IDOR)
findings.remediation_brief: Implement server-side authorisation checks on every request that accesses user-specific data. Never rely on client-supplied IDs as the sole access control mechanism.
findings.description: Data belonging to one user was returned when authenticated as a different user by manipulating object identifiers. This constitutes Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) / Broken Object Level Authorization (BOLA).
findings._x_remediation: Implement server-side authorisation checks on every request that accesses user-specific data. Never rely on client-supplied IDs as the sole access control mechanism.

findings.title: Broken Object Level Authorization (IDOR / BOLA)
findings.remediation_brief: Validate that the authenticated user is authorised to access the requested object on every API call. Use indirect object references or verify ownership server-side.
findings.description: Object-level authorisation is insufficient. Manipulation of object identifiers (IDs, UUIDs, slugs) allows access to resources belonging to other users without being authorised.
findings._x_remediation: Validate that the authenticated user is authorised to access the requested object on every API call. Use indirect object references or verify ownership server-side.

findings.title: Broken Function Level Authorization (BFLA)
findings.remediation_brief: Implement role-based access control checks on every function/endpoint. Deny access by default and explicitly grant it based on user role.
findings.description: Function-level authorisation is insufficient. A lower-privileged user can access administrative or elevated-privilege endpoints by directly requesting them.
findings._x_remediation: Implement role-based access control checks on every function/endpoint. Deny access by default and explicitly grant it based on user role.

findings.title: BFLA: Role Can Access Admin Path
findings.remediation_brief: Restrict all admin paths to authorised roles only. Implement server-side role checks on every request to administrative endpoints.
findings.description: A lower-privileged role was able to access an administrative path. This demonstrates a broken function-level access control vulnerability.
findings._x_remediation: Restrict all admin paths to authorised roles only. Implement server-side role checks on every request to administrative endpoints.

findings.title: Mass Assignment / Privilege Escalation via Parameter Binding
findings.remediation_brief: Explicitly allowlist the parameters that can be bound from user input. Never bind the entire request body to a domain object without filtering.
findings.description: The application binds user-supplied request parameters directly to server-side objects without filtering. This allows attackers to set properties they should not be able to modify, including role, privilege, or verified status.
findings._x_remediation: Explicitly allowlist the parameters that can be bound from user input. Never bind the entire request body to a domain object without filtering.

findings.title: API Endpoint Returns Same Data for All Users
findings.remediation_brief: Implement per-user data filtering at the API layer. Ensure all data responses are scoped to the authenticated user's authorised objects.
findings.description: An API endpoint returns identical data regardless of the authenticated user's identity. This may indicate missing authorisation checks, allowing cross-user data leakage.
findings._x_remediation: Implement per-user data filtering at the API layer. Ensure all data responses are scoped to the authenticated user's authorised objects.

findings.title: Exposed Metrics Endpoint with Sensitive Data
findings.remediation_brief: Restrict metrics endpoints to internal networks or require authentication. Remove sensitive data from metric exports.
findings.description: An application metrics or health check endpoint is publicly accessible and exposes sensitive information such as database credentials, internal hostnames, configuration values, or memory contents.
findings._x_remediation: Restrict metrics endpoints to internal networks or require authentication. Remove sensitive data from metric exports.

findings.title: Business Logic — Hidden Price/Value Field Tampering
findings.remediation_brief: Validate all price and value calculations server-side. Never trust client-supplied price or quantity fields. Recompute values from authoritative server-side data at checkout/submission.
findings.description: A hidden form field or request parameter controlling a monetary or critical value (e.g., price, quantity, discount) can be modified by the client to alter server-side business logic outcomes.
findings._x_remediation: Validate all price and value calculations server-side. Never trust client-supplied price or quantity fields. Recompute values from authoritative server-side data at checkout/submission.

findings.title: Business Logic — Numeric Field Accepts Negative/Zero Value
findings.remediation_brief: Implement server-side range validation for all numeric inputs. Reject negative or zero values where they are not business-valid.
findings.description: A numeric field (e.g., quantity, amount) accepts negative or zero values that the business logic does not validate, potentially enabling free items, credit generation, or account balance manipulation.
findings._x_remediation: Implement server-side range validation for all numeric inputs. Reject negative or zero values where they are not business-valid.

findings.title: Business Logic — Potential Race Condition (Duplicate Submission)
findings.remediation_brief: Implement idempotency tokens for state-changing requests. Use database-level transactions and atomic operations to prevent race conditions.
findings.description: Rapid concurrent submissions of the same request produce responses suggesting duplicate processing. A race condition may allow double-spending, duplicate coupon redemption, or bypassing single-use controls.
findings._x_remediation: Implement idempotency tokens for state-changing requests. Use database-level transactions and atomic operations to prevent race conditions.

findings.title: Business Logic — Workflow Step Directly Accessible
findings.remediation_brief: Enforce workflow state server-side. Verify that all prerequisite steps have been completed before allowing access to subsequent steps. Use server-side state machine validation.
findings.description: A multi-step workflow step is directly accessible without completing preceding steps. This allows skipping of security controls, validation steps, or payment steps in the workflow.
findings._x_remediation: Enforce workflow state server-side. Verify that all prerequisite steps have been completed before allowing access to subsequent steps. Use server-side state machine validation.

findings.title: GraphQL Field Suggestions Enabled
findings.remediation_brief: Disable field suggestions in the GraphQL server configuration (e.g., in Apollo Server, disable suggestions via the formatError hook).
findings.description: GraphQL field suggestions are enabled. When an invalid field name is queried, the server responds with suggestions for similar valid field names. This assists attackers in enumerating the GraphQL schema without introspection access.
findings._x_remediation: Disable field suggestions in the GraphQL server configuration (e.g., in Apollo Server, disable suggestions via the formatError hook).

findings.title: GraphQL Batch Query Attack Possible
findings.remediation_brief: Limit the number of operations allowed in a single GraphQL batch request. Apply per-operation rate limiting.
findings.description: GraphQL batch query execution is enabled without rate limiting. Batching allows multiple operations in a single request, enabling brute-force attacks on authentication fields and bypassing per-request rate limits.
findings._x_remediation: Limit the number of operations allowed in a single GraphQL batch request. Apply per-operation rate limiting.

findings.title: Public Exploit Available
findings.remediation_brief: Apply the relevant security patch or upgrade the affected software component immediately. If patching is not immediately possible, implement compensating controls.
findings.description: A public exploit was found matching an identified software component or version. The existence of a public exploit significantly lowers the bar for an attacker to successfully compromise the application.
findings._x_remediation: Apply the relevant security patch or upgrade the affected software component immediately. If patching is not immediately possible, implement compensating controls.

findings.title: Credentials Transmitted in URL Query Parameters
findings.remediation_brief: Transmit credentials exclusively in the HTTP request body or Authorization header. Never include sensitive values in URLs.
findings.description: Credentials or session tokens were found transmitted in URL query parameters. URL query parameters are stored in browser history, web server logs, and HTTP referer headers, leading to inadvertent credential exposure.
findings._x_remediation: Transmit credentials exclusively in the HTTP request body or Authorization header. Never include sensitive values in URLs.

findings.title: WAF/CDN Possible Session Termination
findings.remediation_brief: Verify that the authenticated session is still valid. If the session was terminated, re-authenticate and resume the scan.
findings.description: An unexpected HTTP status was returned by the target, suggesting a possible session termination by WAF bot-detection heuristics. The authenticated session may no longer be valid.
findings._x_remediation: Verify that the authenticated session is still valid. If the session was terminated, re-authenticate and resume the scan.
